pipeline_name: Western Desert Gas Complex-Ameriya Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: no change; note tier stays medium (single primary source) unless a second independent source surfaces
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE + SPEC, read as a MAP not full text (this cohort's known pattern): the sheet's own cited source (EGAS/GASCO Annual Report 2017/2018, egyptoil-gas.com) is a 36-page PDF; printed page 35 (PDF page index 19) is the GASCO 'National Gas Grid' wall map, confirmed by the page's own printed footer numeral '35'. I extracted the map at native resolution (pdfimages object 2, 1811x2001 CMYK) rather than relying on text extraction. Full-text search of 'Ameriya'/'Amreya'/'Western Desert Gas Complex' in the pdftotext output returns nothing -- expected, not evidence of a bad citation, since this row (like the rest of researcher NA's 40-row cohort) was identified visually off the map. Zoomed 6-10x on the W.D.G. Complex facility icon west of Alexandria: it shows a green (legend = 'EXISTING P/L') line running from the W.D.G. Complex facility icon down to the Borg Elarab/Ameriya-Cement junction node, carrying a leader-line label '24" 26 km' -- printed TWICE, once near each end of the same drawn segment (a normal GASCO-map convention, not two lines). This is an EXACT match to GEM's Diameter=24in, LengthKnown=26.00km, and the GREEN line style (as opposed to the RED 'UNDER CONS. P/L' style used elsewhere on the very same map, e.g. the separate bundle of pipes running north from this same W.D.G. Complex facility toward Abu Homos, which IS drawn in red) confirms Status=operating. This resolves url_verifier's automated flag on the Status ref ('operating' not found in extracted text) -- status here is read from map symbology, not literal text, consistent with the scope brief's explicit test. FuelSource=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both consistent with the map's context (a national gas-transmission grid map) and with this line's role connecting a major gas-processing facility to a distribution hub using the same 'Existing P/L' symbology GASCO uses for its unambiguous trunk lines elsewhere on the map -- nothing suggests a gathering/process-line reclassification.

ATTRIBUTION/LOCATION: StartState/Province='Western Desert' is correct for the W.D.G. Complex facility (it sits in the desert west of the Nile Delta, per the map's own 'WESTERN DESERT' region banner). EndState/Province='Alexandria' is correct -- the Borg Elarab/Ameriya-Cement junction the line terminates at sits within Alexandria Governorate. EndPrefecture/District='Ameriya' (rather than 'Borg El Arab' specifically) is a defensible generalized read: GASREG's own 'Final Approved TNC April 2020' (Section 4.2.4, an independent, later, differently-published source) names the GASCO facility immediately beside W.D.G. Complex on this map as 'El-AMERIA' station -- i.e. 'Ameriya' is this hub's own name in a second official document, not GEM's invention, even though that document's one mention of El-Ameria is on its 32in Dahshour line (P8032), not this 24in/26km line specifically.

DUPLICATE (checked against the full 40-row roster + this row's own PipelineName family): NOT a duplicate of P8031 'Ameriya Cement-Borg El Arab' (12in/14km, a short LOCAL line between the cement plant and the distribution node -- different diameter AND length AND a different, shorter corridor entirely) or P8032 'Ameriya-Dahshour' (32in/200km, heads southeast to Giza, a completely different corridor). P8075 is itself explicitly one of THREE sibling segments of ONE PipelineName ('Western Desert Gas Complex-Ameriya Gas Pipeline'): P8065 'Pipeline I' (24in/15km) and P8066 'Pipeline 2' (12in/14.5km) are the other two, both OUTSIDE this batch's 40-row scope (already-existing rows, not re-audited here). This is GEM's own established convention for multiple physical parallel pipes sharing one name/corridor -- consistent with how the same GASCO map itself bundles multiple diameter/length labels along single drawn corridors elsewhere (e.g. the 5-item red under-construction bundle -- 24"/45km, 18/16"/13km, 12"/14.5km, 24"/15km, 42"/65km -- running north from this same W.D.G. Complex facility toward Abu Homos). Flagging for the record, NOT as a P8075 concern since P8075 itself is clean: that red bundle's two items matching P8065/P8066's exact specs (24"/15km and 12"/14.5km) are drawn in RED ('UNDER CONS. P/L') on this 2018 map and run toward Abu Homos, a different direction from the Borg Elarab/Ameriya-Cement hub P8075 uses -- worth a future look at P8065/P8066's EndPrefecture and 2018-vs-now construction status, but that is their row, not this one's.

SECOND-SOURCE EFFORT: this session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this row was assigned. I fetched the GASREG 'Final Approved TNC April 2020' PDF directly (used successfully for P8032) and full-text-searched it for this line specifically -- it mentions 'El-AMERIA' exactly once, in the Dahshour compressor station section describing the 32in El-Ameria/Dahshour line (P8032's line), and contains no reference to a 24in/26km W.D.G. Complex line. WebFetch attempts at gasreg.org.eg's homepage (403) and two guessed Wikipedia article titles for Al-Amreya/Al-Amriya (both 404) turned up nothing usable. Net result: existence and spec rest on ONE primary, authoritative, GEM-independent source (GASCO's own official national-grid map) rather than two independent sources describing this specific line -- tier is medium, not high, same as the sibling P8031 finding. This is not a GEM-derived value and the source does depict this exact line by name, corridor, and spec; the gap is sourcing depth, not correctness.

summary: P8075 confirmed (caveat): existence, 24in/26km spec, operating status (green 'Existing P/L' on the GASCO map, page 35/PDF p.19), transmission classification, and Western Desert/Alexandria attribution all check out visually against the sheet's own cited GASCO map; not a duplicate of P8031/P8032 or its own sibling segments P8065/P8066 (outside this batch's scope). Tier held at medium -- single primary source, WebSearch budget exhausted and GASREG TNC doesn't cover this specific line -- nothing UNRESOLVED, no fills proposed (Capacity/Owner/StartYear remain genuinely unsupported by any source found, left blank rather than forced).
